message: fix(runtime): a load and a mount publish nothing, and the refusal is measured where it is written

edits.find: The member arrives at `mount`, which is where the seed went, so a loaded node publishes at rest once it is mounted and the asymmetry was never about load at all. It was that a node mounted by a commit is seeded by `#apply` while a node mounted by a caller was seeded by nobody. The seed is at the public verb and never at `#mountNode`, because a commit already seeds the node it mounted. See ADR-066.
edits.replace: The mount does not seed one either, and that half was drafted the other way, implemented and refused by measurement: a seed there contradicts the asymmetry `T-1` owns rather than completing it, it breaks the promise that a time Motion does not emit before its first tick, and because `PatchRegistry.publish` drops a candidate through `samePatch` it would not add a publication but take the next one, leaving the `seek` after a mount handing its caller an empty batch. Run 33712936651 turned 21 cases red on exactly that, `RA-8` among them. So the first real operation on a node carries its first patch, and the asymmetry stays where `T-1` put it. See ADR-066.

edits.find: - A node publishing at rest at the mount: `RA-100` through `RA-102` in `packages/core/test/unit/runtime/mount-flush-seed.test.ts`. `RA-102` is green on purpose as the equivalence half, holding a structural add at exactly one flush, which is what fails if the seed is put at the attach rather than at the public verb. `RA-101` is an oracle rather than a counter, because a sequence that moved proves a flush happened and only a patch proves the flush was about that node.
edits.replace: - What a load and a mount deliberately do not publish: `RA-100` through `RA-102` in `packages/core/test/unit/runtime/mount-flush-seed.test.ts`. All three are green against the state, because the decision is a refusal, and what they would fail without is measured rather than asserted: run 33712639888 is the red run for the seed as first drafted and run 33712936651 is the 21-case measurement that refused it. `RA-101` is the case that fails if either half is added back, and it fails on the publication being taken from the next operation rather than on one being added, which no counter would have caught.

edits.find: so the comparison covers the whole compiled input and `RA-61` is the case the plan read literally would have failed.
edits.replace: so the comparison covers the whole compiled input and `RA-61` is the case the plan read literally would have failed. Part 6 of the re-review is the latest, and the first where the prescription was this project's own audit and the measurement was a `CI` run rather than a reading: it prescribed a flush seed at the mount, and 21 cases across 12 files refused it, because a seed placed in front of a deduplicating publisher takes the next publication rather than adding one. An audit's prescription is measured before it is implemented, and where it is implemented first, the run is the finding.
